thread_analysis.thread_summary: Silex Technology (contact Tetsuya Kuwana) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) for Bluetooth SIG Core Complete module registration referencing NXP RW610/RW612-based QDIDs and the customer's own previously-registered IM-100 module, spanning June through September 2024 -- precisely the period of SIG's major July 2024 registration system overhaul. This thread is unusually rich in foundational technical and historical context about that overhaul, going beyond documenting its symptoms (seen extensively elsewhere in this corpus) to explain its actual root cause.
all_questions_found: Does referencing two existing QDIDs with overlapping RF PHY/LL layer coverage trigger new test requirements, and can this be avoided if the overlapping content is identical? (see thread_0047_case_01)
What caused the July 2024 registration system overhaul to expand Consistency Check to cover previously-excluded referenced existing registrations? (see thread_0047_case_02)

(Administrative/technical, not separately cased) A related but more advanced technique -- substituting one referenced QDID's RF PHY/LL layers with another compatible QDID's corresponding layers (rather than simply choosing the broader reference) -- was used to combine a Component QDID with the customer's own IM-100 module's Controller Subsystem without triggering lower-layer test requirements; this is a more specific application of case_01's underlying principle. Also: standard quote/order/Review-Page/Submission administrative flow, and confirmation of the post-Submission 'reviewed and approved' green-bar indicator versus a possible 'Submission Rejected' notification email.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_02 is one of the most valuable pieces of foundational context in this entire corpus: while many other threads document the SYMPTOMS of the July 2024 registration overhaul (full-hierarchy Consistency Check, expanded IOPT testing, elimination of certain registration shortcuts), this thread captures the actual ROOT CAUSE directly from a SIG representative -- a Core Specification v6.0+ compatibility gap with older v4.0-Mandatory-only BLE lower-layer implementations. Case_01 provides a concrete, reusable technique (checking for ICS content identity across overlapping QDID references) for avoiding unnecessary new test requirements when multiple existing registrations are combined.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0047_case_01 and thread_0047_case_02 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_01's risk is committing to an unnecessarily complex and costly multi-QDID reference structure without checking for a simpler equivalent.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified -- the consultant proactively ran trial registrations in his own Workspace to test alternative reference structures before committing the customer to either path, and transparently explained that even a BQTF-accredited facility was still working through the new system's case-by-case complexity rather than overstating confidence in a clean general rule.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When educating customers about the July 2024 registration overhaul, go beyond listing the official reference resources (QPRDv3, SIG's webinar, the FAQ page) to explain the underlying Core Specification v6.0+ compatibility-gap rationale, since this context helps customers understand why their specific test requirements may be unpredictable; and when a customer wants to reference multiple existing QDIDs with overlapping layer coverage, always check whether the overlapping content is actually identical before assuming the more complex multi-reference structure is necessary.
